findings.evidence: caption: 'Unilateral periorbitaledema without conjunctivitis noted in child with TRAPS during flares'

panels.rationale: Clinical photograph demonstrating unilateral periorbital edema in a pediatric patient with TRAPS, explicitly identified in the caption.

in_text_mentions: 34 had recurrent episodes of fever lasting for 2–3 weeks every 3–4 months with rash since 18 months of age. These f episodes were associated with pain abdomen, myalgias, arthritis, periorbital edema (Figure 6), and subcutaneous swellings. She had received multiple courses of antimicrobials in view of marked polymorphonuclear leukocytosis. Her father was also symptomatic and used to have fever and intermittent subcutaneous swelling and rash. Father was diagnosed to have acute rheumatic fever in childhood.
